summary: The University of Illinois Center for Advanced Computation proposes graphic display modes for its ARPANET node. Unlike other nodes, it was setting up a system for the ILLIAC IV and the network, so it was building its graphics system from scratch.

plainLanguage.summary: The University of Illinois describes display operations it wants a network graphics protocol to support. It gives particular attention to four ways of representing shaded or raster images.

what display modes did rfc 184 propose

subtitle: A proposal for standard and specialized display modes in a graphics protocol.

tldr.problem: The University of Illinois was building graphics software for a new network node and wanted to identify display modes for a network graphics protocol.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists common display operations and describes four proposed grey-level modes: GRIDAREA, MATRIXAREA, SCANLINE and SCANPOINT.
tldr.outcome: The report shares Illinois's initial design ideas and invites discussion with other network sites.

today: RFC 184 is a graphics display-mode proposal published in July 1971. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: Graphics Protocol Needs
sections.content:
Illinois was building a computer system for the ILLIAC IV and the network, including graphics software. Because its graphics system was being developed from the ground up, the team wanted its data structures and files to work with the emerging Network Graphics Protocol.

The RFC asks other network nodes to discuss which display modes should be included. It names points, lines, vectors, character streams, viewport and window specifications, transformations, equipment-specific byte streams and input read-back.
sections.plainLanguage: Illinois was building a new graphics system and wanted it to work across the network. It listed basic drawing, text, view control, device-specific data and user input as needs.

sections.title: Grey-Level Modes
sections.content:
GRIDAREA defines a grid and intensity range, then assigns an intensity to selected cells. MATRIXAREA fills a raster display with user-defined pseudo-characters. SCANLINE sends the starting point and each change in intensity as a scan moves across rows.

SCANPOINT also advances the scan automatically, but requires a separate intensity value for every point. The RFC describes these modes for grey-level displays and related raster output.
sections.plainLanguage: GRIDAREA shades selected cells, while MATRIXAREA uses dot patterns. SCANLINE sends only changes in shade, and SCANPOINT sends the shade for each point.

sections.title: Device Flexibility
sections.content:
The proposal recognizes that graphics equipment differs. A point or line may be drawn differently by a plotter and an interactive display. The protocol should also allow equipment-specific byte streams, even though other nodes might not understand those special commands.

Input from devices such as joysticks, cursors and light pens is also device-dependent. The RFC calls for the protocol to account for these differences while supporting common display elements.
sections.plainLanguage: Different devices may draw the same picture in different ways. The protocol should support shared operations and allow special data for equipment that needs it.
